own_scenes.desc: Desde Sugar Hill, Nueva Jersey pesó en el hip hop: la Flavor Unit de Mark the 45 King (Queen Latifah, Chill Rob G, Lakim Shabazz); Latifah convenció a los New Style de East Orange de llamarse Naughty by Nature. Luego vino una segunda ola: Redman (aliado de EPMD), Lords of the Underground (DoItAll, Mr. Funke y DJ Lord Jazz, de la Universidad de Shaw, producidos por Marley Marl en su «House of Hits»), Artifacts, Das EFX, Outsidaz y Rah Digga; Just Blaze pinchaba sus propias bases en las noches de micro abierto del Pipeline de Newark. Casi todos entraron aliándose con grupos de Nueva York. Los Fugees (Wyclef Jean, Lauryn Hill, Pras) mezclaron reggae, rap y R&B con instrumentos en Ruffhouse: Blunted on Reality (1994) y The Score (1996), Grammy al mejor disco de rap, con «Fu-Gee-La» (una base que Fat Joe rechazó), «Killing Me Softly» y «Ready or Not»: Lauryn Hill, entre las mejores MCs de la historia.

refs.q: That’s what sold it. It was completely different from everything.
refs.para: Chris Schwartz (cofounder, Ruffhouse): When they first auditioned for us in [Steven] Soderbergh’s office, it was a hot mess. But, for me, what was really important was that Wyclef was playing an acoustic guitar over a beatbox. That’s what sold it. It was completely different from everything.

refs.q: Even though it was hard for us to break in, most of the New Jersey acts, we broke in by teaming up with New York crews.
refs.para: Dupré “DoItAll” Kelly (artist, Lords of the Underground): You had all of those Jersey crews in the ’90s from Queen Latifah to Apache to Naughty by Nature to Redman, Lords of the Underground, Rah Digga, the Artifacts. Even though it was hard for us to break in, most of the New Jersey acts, we broke in by teaming up with New York crews. Lords of the Underground, Marley Marl. That’s the House of Hits and everybody came to that house, from Heavy D to LL Cool J to TLC.
